parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Identify one cause of migration from Source 1.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Using Source 2, identify one consequence of migration for the country people are moving
to.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Which consequence of migration do you think is the most significant? Explain why.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Using Sources 1 and 2, explain why migration is an important issue for countries.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
‘We must help the refugees.’
What are the strengths and weaknesses of the argument supporting this claim?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘Migrants help the economy of a country to grow stronger.’
How could you test this claim? You may consider the types of information, sources of evidence
or methods you might use.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Identify an example of a vested interest in Source 4. Explain why this is a vested interest.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Which argument is more convincing, Isa’s or Jusse’s?
Your answer should consider both arguments and you should support your point of view with
their words.
You should also consider:
• the strength of their reasoning and evidence
• their use of language
• the different types of information used.

text: ‘Governments should allow people to migrate between countries if they want to.’ Do you agree
• give reasons and evidence to support your opinion
• use the material in the sources and/or any of your own ideas
